title: restic 0.18.0 on NetBSD 10.1 throws xattr errors when filesystem doesn't do xattrs....

Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
restic 0.18.0 compiled with go1.24.1 on netbsd/amd64


What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------
rest-server


Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------
Every file on the filesystem that is being considered for backup throws an error like:
...
error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd2l: xattr.list /dev/rwd2l: operation not supported                          16:11:13 [1418/1891]
error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd2m: xattr.list /dev/rwd2m: operation not supported                                              error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd2n: xattr.list /dev/rwd2n: operation not supported                                              
error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd2o: xattr.list /dev/rwd2o: operation not supported                                              error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd2p: xattr.list /dev/rwd2p: operation not supported                                              
error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd3a: xattr.list /dev/rwd3a: operation not supported                                              error: incomplete metadata for /dev/rwd3b: xattr.list /dev/rwd3b: operation not supported                                              
...
error: incomplete metadata for /var/yp: xattr.list /var/yp: operation not supported
error: incomplete metadata for /var/yp/Makefile.main: xattr.list /var/yp/Makefile.main: operation not supported
error: incomplete metadata for /var/yp/Makefile.yp: xattr.list /var/yp/Makefile.yp: operation not supported
error: incomplete metadata for /var/yp/binding: xattr.list /var/yp/binding: operation not supported
error: incomplete metadata for /var/yp/nicknames: xattr.list /var/yp/nicknames: operation not supported
...
Basically if the file is on the filesystem, there is an error produced for it.
Version 0.17.3 worked just fine.  Version 0.18.0 spews errors.
I don't think RESTIC_REPOSITORY and RESTIC_PASSWORD variable content are overly relevant here, as those worked fine with 0.17.3 and are consistent with what are used for similar backups with Linux hosts.  The back-ends are running rest-server (I see the issue on multiple NetBSD boxes, with two different rest-server back-ends).

The filesystems on the NetBSD boxes looks like (just one example, the others are similar):
file system: /dev/rraid1a
format  FFSv1
endian  little-endian
magic   11954           time    Wed Apr  2 16:14:15 2025
superblock location     8192    id      [ 61b9319f 3dc140e ]

nindir  4096    inopb   128

sblkno  8       cblkno  16      iblkno  24      dblkno  1480
sbsize  2048    cgsize  16384
csaddr  1480    cssize  4096
cgrotor 0       fmod    0       ronly   0       clean   0x02
wapbl version 0x1       location 2      flags 0x0
wapbl loc0 40007808     loc1 76896      loc2 512        loc3 3
usrquota 0      grpquota 0
flags   wapbl 
fsmnt   /
volname         swuid   0


I'll note that it's using FFSv2, and not FFSv2ea which would actually support the extended attributes.
I'm able to repeat this on 4 different NetBSD 10.0 systems, all running non-FFSv2ea filesystems, and all of which backed up perfectly with 0.17.3.

On one of the systems the nighly backup seemed to completely fail when run in automated fashion.  They do seem to succeed in the end, albeit with very very noisy output of one error per file encountered.

Backup line reproducer looks like:
restic backup --one-file-system /
Problem is 100% reproducible for me (with 2 different rest-server back-ends).  One system didn't send its usual backup report, which was how the issue was discovered. Other systems did send a report, looking normal, until we ran backups by hand and found that the xattr errors were being spewed there too.  Unknown why the one system didn't actually complete the backup -- perhaps the backup summary (which also then contained one very long error line per file, with about 1 million files) didn't make it through the email system?

Reverting to 0.17.3 has everthing working fine again.

Enabling xattrs on NetBSD, but the code not actually checking to see if the filesystem actually supports xattrs?  I havn't had a chance to dig into https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5174 to see what changed.  Again, things work flawlessly with 0.17.3, but fail with 0.18.0.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant2 Care to have a stab at fixing this? :)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I suspect that it's as designed, since it behaves the same way, on Linux, when I use it on file systems that don't support xattrs, like SSHFS, ISO9660, and NetATalk volumes, hosted on older platforms, like NetWare, that don't support them.

I haven't looked too deeply, but the codepath, inside Restic, should be identical, to that, on FreeBSD, since the API is the same, as is the GoLang veneer.

Extended attribute support is an opt-in feature, that needs a file system that supports them (UFS/FFS has an option, to enable it, if I remember correctly, and ZFS *might* support it, but I haven't got a NetBSD machine to hand, at the moment).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: (My original change that enables extended attributes, was a literal one-liner, but some refactoring of my patch was done, to make extended attributes support more generic, so I suspect it's mostly a "cosmetic", or "cultural" issue, since extended attributes weren't in widespread use, on NetBSD, for a long time, so no-one really gave much testing, to that infrastructure).

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I'll likely have a look, at the xattr-handling code, when I get chance, and see if there's any way of at least silencing the error, but I can't guarantee if/when I can spin, and test another patch, though. :)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I had a bit more time today to dig into this... It seems that perhaps EOPNOTSUPP just needs to be handled/ignored?
https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5344
With that pullup 0.18.0 once again works on a FFSv2 filesystem on NetBSD without xattr.  I havn't checked, but this may also fix errors thrown on ISO9660 or other filesystems.

I only did brief testing with this patch, but it also fixes errors seen with restore on NetBSD with 0.18.0 as well:
...
ignoring error for /root: xattr.list /tmp/b/root: operation not supported
Summary: Restored 118 / 143 files/dirs (2.705 MiB / 2.705 MiB) in 0:00
Fatal: There were 144 errors

Someone(TM) will want to test this more thoroughly, and make sure the fix is appropriate.
Thanks!

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I hit a similar 18.0 regression when backing up to a filesystem that didn’t support chmod. Here’s [my fix](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5345/files ) for that.

18.0 uses a newer version of Go yeah? I’m guessing that started surfacing not-supported errors more often.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
No, it's FFSv2:
```
file system: /dev/dk8
format  FFSv2
endian  little-endian
...
```
For the backup, restic runs as non-root, in case it matters.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Ahh... ok, now I can replicate what you're seeing.   Yes, it matters if root or not :) 
So in versions before 0.18.0, it looks like restic simply skips over devices and you don't get a 'permission denied' when doing a non-root backup (you get 'permission denied' for files/dirs tho).

Now, it's looking for xattr.list before doing some sort of device check, and then getting the permission denied on reading the xattr.list file (even though that file won't actually exist either!).

Not sure (yet) if there is a workaround for this error message.
